description: Stock Market - What to do now and later
body_html:
Normally, I like to record a video, put my face to my thoughts. But this morning when I sat down to record…I kind of just looked blankly at my notes and the camera. My Nvidia research this weekend, was largely at the forefront of my mind. If you didn’t see it, it is linked down below (please watch it before continuing to read). Three thoughts, somewhat connected came to mind:

  1. The Enron & Nvidia comparison, counter arguments and hate comments.

  2. What can we do NOW as investors?

  3. What do I think will perform well in the next bull market?

A written post seemed more appropriate for this Frankenstein of thoughts mashed together…

Please read this and leave your comments below…I am seeking constructive feedback!

People were not happy about me comparing Nvidia to Enron…

And I couldn’t care less.

Whenever I post a negative or bearish post, I am mentally prepared for backlash. Heck, I started my content creator journey, years ago, saying crypto (Ethereum) was going to go into a bear market…the hate is engagement, which caused virality, and hence the initial rise up the social media ladder. Crypto went into a solid bear market for several months soon after those posts. The same thing happened last December 2024, when I got out of the market and called for a stock market crash. I didn’t know at the time if it would be the meltdown or not…in February I posted that it was NOT the melt down. But again, regardless, I received a lot of hate…which preceded a technical bear market, though relatively short, it was pretty extreme.

So why am I sharing stories of the past about engagement on social media? Because it is a signal 🚨. I have learned to recognize that the more hatred I receive, the higher the likelihood the post is accurate. I could give dozens more examples. But think about it…out of 1510 comments…all of the hate is emotionally charged. I did not see a single solid counter argument. The two comments that are somewhat relevant:

  1. You cannot compare Enron to Nvidia. They are different. Apples to Oranges.

    1. I respectfully disagree. If apples are facing a drought or supply chain issues…then its likely oranges are too. They are different…but lessons can be learned from one, so as to not make the same mistakes with the other.

  2. Enron was a fraud and didn’t generate revenue like Nvidia does. Nvidia produces real products.

    1. Enron was reporting revenues of over $150B1 before all of the fraud was discovered. As the yahoo message board clearly showed, at that time, the people thought it was legitimate. To be honest, I don’t think Nvidia is a “bad” company…or even committing fraud necessarily. I just think the numbers are inflated, riding on hopes and dreams of future sales…that may or may not come. They make 1/3 the revenue of Apple and Microsoft, but have 25% more market cap? Makes no sense. I also agree with the comment above about circular financing. That has already been shown in the in the entire AI sector.

The primary point: There hasn’t been any really great counter arguments to the comparison. Just emotionally charged retail investors. Thus, my stance, remains.

So what do we do now as investors?

Whatever you want to do. I’m just a retail investor, just like you, that enjoys doing market analysis and posting on the internet. However…for ME:

If you watch the entire video (it drives me INSANE people who don’t have a 3 minute attention span, but have lots to say, toughly 😒)…I talk about IF NVIDIA IS FOLLOWING THE SAME TRAJECTORY AS ENRON…then I think it has another leg. Meaning:

  • I will have to cut my short position, wait for a leg up, then enter at a break in the uptrend. At the end of the day, regardless of speculation, PRICE ACTION IS KING!

  • So why not go long? For what? 10%? 15%? MAYBE? No. I doubt ill be able to time that top…or ride that trend for very long. When I entered positions in 2022 and 2023…it was because I was confident we had a long runway ahead of us. I do not chase 10% gains. But after 50% or 100% potential (I achieved 142% portfolio gain for 2024, receipts posted). I contemplate a much larger risk, than there is profit potential. I have made enough the last 3 years. June to September was pretty solid this year. I am fine. Plus…we are coming up on the holidays. I would like to enjoy them, not stare at a chart barely moving.

The point being: I don’t want to do anything. Too much risk, not enough potential profit. Lots of work, for pennies.

So what about the future?

You can’t, and I won’t, stay a bear forever. Its silly and biased. I got lots of hate in 2022 for being bullish and calling for a melt up (the inverse of what I receive today). My mind is already gravitating to the next bull market. When all these new retail investors and profound bull market genius influencers are wiped away, then there will be new assets to buy. That is a far away though. Of course I will have a few shorts running…but it is certainly not the “big money” a bull market provides. Shorts are fun, keep the bear market bearable and keeps you in tune with the market.

When and if the market breaks, I will begin monitoring for future winners. I didn’t pull Palantir or Roblox out of a magic hat 🪄🎩. Back in 2022, they showed signs of heavy resistance. Yes, they went down. But there were signs of accumulation, signs of money creeping in, along with many others. They went down less than other assets.

Additionally… assets I am watching: Oil and Treasury bonds

  • People have been fighting me on my Oil forecast for 2 years now….and losing. My stance remains that it will go to ~$30 a barrel. Even with that bearish outlook, presently, I think oil will be the next major price action leader in the next bull market. This article is getting lengthy…I’ll re-present my thesis in the near future.

  • 20+ Year treasury bonds I also think are carving out a bottom. I have not yet seen the price action bounces that I normally like, so am still waiting. But I do strongly suspect that I will go through an accumulation phase myself, and hold onto TLT for a while.

    See? Not all bearish. More so realistic. Unfortunately, neither of these assets are “ready” in my opinion. So I would rather preserve capital for them, and others, down the line.

Kind of all over the place with thoughts today. If you have questions, feel free to stop by the chat and ask. I am available during market hours. Hope you have a great day, and… THANKS FOR STOPPING BY!
